Let G be a finite group and let p be a prime divisor of [G[. Let T = {xeGlxP= 1}.
It is known ([2]) that if G is not a p-group then irf<

is, for Mersenne primes, best possible. For p = 2 it is easy to check that if G is a
2-group not of exponent 2, then [TI<3[Gt and this bound is attained e.g. in
the dihedral group of order 8. In this note we show that rTI<~IGI when G is
a 3-group not of exponent 3 and again this bound is best possible. This answers
a question posed by MacHale. The negative solution to the Hughes Hp-problem
([3]) suggests that no result of this type (i.e. IT[ < k lGI where k < 1 (k independent
of G)) is likely for G a p-group not of exponent p for p > 3.
     The notation is standard (c.f. [1]).
